sources.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Ch. 11 §11.4, printed pp. 16–20
sources.locator: Complete 78-page Chapter 11 PDF; full relevant reasoning in §§11.3–11.4, printed pp. 15–20 (PDF pp. 15–20), equations (11.12)–(11.19) and Algorithm 11.1.

contents.name: Detailed balance and the symmetric-flow condition, §11.3, equations (11.12)–(11.15), printed pp. 15–16
contents.reason: Read the complete finite-state argument. The authored theorem gives the required general-state measure proof locally rather than importing the source's discrete derivation.

contents.name: Metropolis–Hastings acceptance ratio from balancing proposal flows, §11.4, equations (11.16)–(11.19), printed pp. 17–18
contents.reason: The source derives the common-density ratio and discusses zero forward-proposal mass. The authored lemma separately derives it from the general accepted-flow construction.

contents.name: Accept/reject procedure and rejected value retained, §11.4 and Algorithm 11.1, printed pp. 16–20
contents.reason: The complete procedure section was read; the local algorithm uses a general proposal kernel and explicitly retains rejected mass at the current state.

contents.name: Symmetric random walk on an undirected graph, Example 11.1, printed p. 16
contents.reason: Used to check the symmetric-proposal convention; the three-state target and all transition entries are calculated locally.

contents.name: Rejected proposals remain in the sample, §11.4, printed pp. 19–20
contents.reason: The source explicitly distinguishes valid rejection self-transitions from incorrectly dropping repeated states; the finite two-state calculation is local.

sources.retrieval_history: The browser PDF viewer initially returned 403. Search located alternate full-text treatments; a direct curl recovery of this same author-hosted URL returned HTTP 200 and a 1,909,243-byte PDF. The complete 78-page chapter was extracted, and §§11.3–11.4 were read in full.

sources.title: Gareth O. Roberts and Jeffrey S. Rosenthal, General State Space Markov Chains and MCMC Algorithms, §2.1 and Proposition 2, printed pp. 4–6
sources.locator: Complete 64-page author-hosted PDF; relevant complete algorithm discussion and Proposition 2 proof in §2.1, printed pp. 4–6 (PDF pp. 4–5).

contents.name: General MCMC setup and reversible-kernel motivation, §2 and Proposition 1, printed pp. 4–5
contents.reason: Read the full proposition and proof in the source. Its density-based argument is used as an independent check; the local proof supplies the general measure-level symmetric-flow argument.

contents.name: Metropolis–Hastings proposal, acceptance probability, and detailed-balance proof, §2.1 and Proposition 2, printed pp. 5–6
contents.reason: Read the complete relevant proof. The local carriers extend the proposal-flow construction beyond the source's density presentation and preserve its rejected self-loop.

contents.name: Common-density forward/reverse proposal ratio, §2.1, printed pp. 5–6
contents.reason: The source confirms the ratio orientation; its hypotheses are not used as a substitute for the local measure-flow proof.

sources.title: John K. Hunter, Measure Theory, Theorem 6.27 and proof, §6.8, printed pp. 75–77
sources.locator: Complete 93-page notes. Inspected the finite-measure construction and uniqueness proof in Theorem 6.27, §6.8, printed pp. 75–76 (PDF pp. 79–80), plus the sigma-finite reduction on printed p. 77. The latter contains a typographical error in the displayed singular-component sum and is not used as evidence for that step.

contents.name: Finite-measure Radon–Nikodym construction and uniqueness, Theorem 6.27, printed pp. 75–77
contents.reason: The inspected finite-measure RN construction and uniqueness proof supply the density interface used by the local meet lemma; the pointwise minimum and bounded acceptance-version arguments are proved locally.

contents.name: Finite common-submeasure formula for two measures with densities, Theorem 6.27 and proof, printed pp. 75–77
contents.reason: The finite-measure RN construction supplies the density ingredient. The arbitrary sigma-finite reference case uses the complete local positive-density RN supplier; the printed typo in Hunter p. 77 is not used. The local item proves the minimum-density and greatestness claims.
